member.name: T:MGUI.Core.UI.Brushes.Border_Brushes.MGBorderBand
member.param:
Determines how much thickness this band will be drawn with.
EX: If drawing the entire with =10, and there are 2 bands with weights of 0.4 and 0.6,
the 1st band is drawn with Floor(10*(0.4/(0.4+0.6))=4, 2nd band is drawn with Floor(10*(0.6/(0.4+0.6))=6 thickness.
(Weights do not need to sum to 1.0)
Warning - the actual thickness is always rounded down, so the total rendered size of the border may end up less than the it was drawn with.

member.summary:
Determines what percentage of the current animation cycle is complete. Min = 0.0 (0%), Max = 1.0 (100%)
For example, if is set to , one cycle represents showing the highlight for a set amount of time, then hiding for a set amount of time.
Note: For , this progress value represents where the CENTER of the highlight should appear on the perimeter. 0.0 = topleft, 0.50 = bottomright etc.
member.remarks:
If this value is not in the range [0.0,1.0], only the decimal portion is used. EX: 2.35 is equivalent to 0.35.

member.name: M:MGUI.Core.UI.Containers.Grids.MGGrid.NormalizeWeightedLengths
member.summary:
Converts all weighted row/column lengths to integral values that are clamped between the Min/Max size of the row/column.
For example, if the columns are:
Index Length MinWidth MaxWidth ActualWidth 0 1* 20 50 50 1 25px null null 25 2 1.2* 30 100 80
Grid total width: 155
Normalizing the weights would convert the columns to:
Index Length MinWidth MaxWidth ActualWidth 0 50* 20 50 50 1 25px null null 25 2 80* 30 100 80
Grid total width: 155
This method is typically only used when simplifying the row/column definitions before applying resizing logic, such as in .

member.name: T:MGUI.Core.UI.Containers.VirtualizingStackPanel
member.summary:
A vertical stack panel that only creates and maintains UI elements for items currently visible in the viewport, dramatically reducing memory and CPU cost for large lists.
Items outside the viewport are recycled and returned to a pool. Items entering the viewport are either dequeued from the pool or freshly created via .
Only supports a vertical (top-to-bottom) orientation with a uniform item height ().

member.summary: The total number of logical items in the virtual list (including those not yet created as UI elements).

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.Containers.VirtualizingStackPanel.UniformItemHeight
member.summary:
The height (in pixels) of each item. All items must have the same height.
Default value: 24

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.Containers.VirtualizingStackPanel.BufferCount
member.summary:
The number of additional items to realize above and below the visible viewport. A small buffer prevents flickering during fast scrolling.
Default value: 2

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.Containers.VirtualizingStackPanel.ItemGenerator
member.summary:
Invoked when a logical item needs to be presented in the viewport.
The returned will be added as a child of this panel and positioned at the correct layout bounds.
The caller may check to obtain a previously-recycled element instead of creating a new one, then update its content to reflect the new logical item.

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.Containers.VirtualizingStackPanel.ItemRecycler
member.summary: Invoked just before a realized item is removed from the visual tree and placed back in the recycle pool. The caller should unbind data, reset state, etc.

member.summary:

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.Data_Binding.XAMLBindableBase.Bindings
member.summary:
This property is used to temporarily store data on objects while they are being parsed from XAML.
Most MGUI elements have middleman objects that XAML is first parsed to (such as MGUI.Core.UI.XAML.Button), and then those middleman objects are later converted to the underlying type (such as MGUI.Core.UI.MGButton) after the entire XAML string is done parsing. s cannot be instantiated until after the entire window's XAML content is parsed/post-processed (otherwise the source object of the data-binding wouldn't exist yet and ElementName references might not be resolvable).
So this property allows temporarily storing the necessary binding data during parsing, then copying it to the underlying type after it's created, then creating the binding after all other window content is done processing.

member.summary: Specifies the visibility of a ScrollBar for scrollable content.

member.name: F:MGUI.Core.UI.ScrollBarVisibility.Disabled
member.summary:
A ScrollBar does not appear even when the viewport cannot display all of the content.
The content is not allocated infinite space in the ScrollBar's dimension, and instead only receives the space of the viewport.
ScrollBar Layout Size: Zero
ScrollBar Render Size: Zero
Content AvailableSpace: Same as Viewport

member.name: F:MGUI.Core.UI.ScrollBarVisibility.Auto
member.summary:
A ScrollBar appears if the viewport cannot display all of the content. The content is allocated infinite space in the ScrollBar's dimension.
If Content fits within Viewport:
ScrollBar Layout Size: Zero
ScrollBar Render Size: Zero
Content AvailableSpace: Infinite
If Content does not fit within Viewport:
ScrollBar Layout Size: Non-Zero
ScrollBar Render Size: Non-Zero
Content AvailableSpace: Infinite

member.name: F:MGUI.Core.UI.ScrollBarVisibility.Hidden
member.summary:
A ScrollBar does not appear, even when the viewport cannot display all of the content, but the ScrollBar still consumes space in the layout.
The content is allocated infinite space in the ScrollBar's dimension.
This value is typically only used if you want to render your own ScrollBar, while having the ScrollBar's layout bounds reserved for you. Otherwise, consider using instead.
ScrollBar Layout Size: Non-Zero
ScrollBar Render Size: Zero
Content AvailableSpace: Infinite

member.name: F:MGUI.Core.UI.ScrollBarVisibility.Visible
member.summary:
A ScrollBar always appears, even if the viewport can display all of the content. The content is allocated infinite space in the ScrollBar's dimension.
ScrollBar Layout Size: Non-Zero
ScrollBar Render Size: Non-Zero
Content AvailableSpace: Infinite

member.name: F:MGUI.Core.UI.ScrollBarVisibility.Collapsed
member.summary:
A ScrollBar does not appear, even when the viewport cannot display all of the content. The content is allocated infinite space in the ScrollBar's dimension.
ScrollBar Layout Size: Zero
ScrollBar Render Size: Zero
Content AvailableSpace: Infinite

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.MGChatBox.TimestampFormat
member.summary:
A format string used to compute the text to display for each message's ()
Default value: @"'\\['HH:mm:ss']'", which displays the hours/minutes/seconds surrounded by brackets, such as: "[14:33:20]"
Note: Single quotes can be used as an escape character to insert any text you wish, such as: @"'[color=Red] \\[ [b]' HH:mm:ss '[/b] ] [/color]'"
Which would result in the entire timestamp text being red, with the hour/minutes/seconds surrounded by brackets and rendered in bold font.
Note that the open bracket '[' is a special character that typically indicates the start of a text formatting code.
If you want to use an open bracket literally, you must escape the inlined markdown by prefixing the open bracket with 2 backslash literals ('\\\\' or @"\\")

member.name: E:MGUI.Core.UI.MGContextMenu.ContextMenuOpening
member.summary:
Fired just before this is shown, after has run.
Set to to prevent the menu from opening.
Dynamic items: Use instead of subscribing here to add/clear items. is called automatically on every open (before this event fires) and avoids the risks below.
Double-subscription warning: This is a standard C# event — subscribing N times means the handler runs N times per open. If the same object re-subscribes on every tab-rebuild or layout pass, items (or other side-effects) will accumulate. Always pair a subscription with an unsubscription, or use which replaces the handler pattern entirely.
Recommended patterns:
Static items: declare them once in XAML or in the constructor — no handler needed.
Dynamic items: set once.
Conditional logic (not item-building): subscribe here, but ensure you unsubscribe when the hosting element is disposed / rebuilt.

member.name: M:MGUI.Core.UI.MGDesktop.RecalculateTextLayouts
member.summary:
Re-resolves all font handles from the currently active and invalidates their layout and measurement caches.
Call this after switching at runtime so that the new engine's metrics (e.g. different scale factors or glyph data) are reflected immediately on every text element across all windows.
After re-resolving all font handles, also calls to flush any stale cached measurements on container elements that depend on text sizes, ensuring the next frame re-measures the full layout tree with the new engine's metrics.

member.summary:
Manages 1 or more s, allowing you to define overlay(s) overtop of a piece of content. The overlays span the same bounds and scope as this .
Although you could just use an to achieve similar results, s provides a more convenient and specialized use-case.
For example, this class can guarantee that no inputs fall-through to content underneath the overlay (=). It also ensures that, if there are multiple overlays for the same content, at most only 1 of them will be visibile/interactable at a time.

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.MGTextBox.CharacterLimit
member.summary:
The maximum # of characters that can be inputted in this . Use null for no character limit.
Some characters are automatically added to this ,
such as hyphens that are appended at the end of a line when a single word's width exceeds the line's width and the word must wrap across multiple lines.
These characters do not count towards the limit.
Linebreaks count as 1 character ('\n'). Tabs are typically treated as 4 spaces and thus count as 4 characters. See also:

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.MGTextBox.LimitedCharacterCountFormatString
member.summary:
Only relevant if is true and is not null.
A format string to use when computing the character-count text displayed in the bottom-right corner of this .
"{{CharacterCount}}" and "{{CharacterLimit}}" will be replaced with their actual underlying values when formatting the string.
Default value:"[b]{{CharacterCount}}[/b] / [b]{{CharacterLimit}}[/b]"
This value supports some basic text markdown, such as "[b]" for bold text, "[fg=Red]" to set the text foreground color to a given value, "[opacity=0.5]" etc.
See also: , ,

member.name: P:MGUI.Core.UI.ThemeFontSettings.UseExactScale
member.summary:
If true, will attempt to draw text with a scale that most closely results in the desired font size.
If false, may choose a slightly different font size that approximates the exact size, but results in better scaling results.
For example, if you have SpriteFonts for these font sizes: 8, 10, 12, and you wanted to use font size = 19
If is true: would choose size=10, scale=1.9
If is false: would choose size=10, scale=2.0, preferring to scale by values such as 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 etc
Default value: false

member.name: M:MGUI.Core.UI.Text.MGTextLine.#ctor(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{MGUI.Core.UI.Text.MGTextRun},System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Int32})
member.param:
The indices of the original character that each character in the lines corresponds to. Only used for very specific purposes.
EX: If input is a run with Text = "ABC12345", and that text couldn't fit on a single line, it may be split to something like: [ "ABC12-", "345" ]
Notice that a '-' character was automatically inserted at the end of the first line, so now the wrapped text at index=5 is '-', while the wrapped text in the input "ABC12345" at index=5 is '3'.
So the indices mapping in this case would be: [ 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7 ]
This parameter is intended to know to which character in the original input corresponds to each character in the wrapped output.

member.name: M:MGUI.Core.UI.Text.MGTextLine.ParseLines(MGUI.Core.UI.Text.ITextMeasurer,System.Double,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{MGUI.Core.UI.Text.MGTextRun},System.Boolean)
member.param:
If true, lines consisting of only a single space character will be ignored, unless it is the first line or if it immediately follows a linebreak.
For example, if the line could fit exactly 5 characters, and the text is "Hello World", the result would normally be:
-------
|Hello|
| ....| (This line only contains a space)
|World|
------- If is true, it would instead result in:
-------
|Hello|
|World|
------- Note that lines consisting of multiple consecutive spaces will still be returned.

member.name: M:MGUI.Core.UI.Text.MGTextLine.ParseLines(MGUI.Core.UI.Text.ITextMeasurer,System.Double,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{MGUI.Core.UI.Text.MGTextRun},System.Boolean,System.Char[])
member.param:
If true, lines consisting of only a single space character will be ignored, unless it is the first line or if it immediately follows a linebreak.
For example, if the line could fit exactly 5 characters, and the text is "Hello World", the result would normally be:
-------
|Hello|
| ....| (This line only contains a space)
|World|
------- If is true, it would instead result in:
-------
|Hello|
|World|
------- Note that lines consisting of multiple consecutive spaces will still be returned.
Recommended: ' ' (space) and '-' (hyphen)
member.remarks:
Known non-idempotency issue (PR #35):
The wrapping decision uses a word-by-word accumulated width (CurrentX), while the resulting is computed by re-measuring each run as a complete string inside FlushLine.
Because a whole-string measurement can be smaller than the sum of its word-by-word measurements (inter-glyph kerning), calling ParseLines(W) may produce a line with LineWidth = W' < W. Calling ParseLines(W') then wraps again, because the per-word sum still exceeds W'.
Fix: align the wrapping decision with FlushLine by measuring the candidate line as a whole string before deciding whether to wrap.
